arxiv-2203-01942.title: The Maximum Isotropic Equivalent Energy Of Gamma Ray Bursts
arxiv-2203-01942.creator: Shlomo Dado, Arnon Dar
arxiv-2203-01942.description: Abstract The canonball model, which unifies cosmic ray bursts (CRBs) and gamma ray bursts (GRBs), is used to predict the maximum isotropic equivalent gamma ray energy release in a GRB. The predicted maximum is based on the observed knee around 1 TeV in the energy spectrum of Galactic cosmic ray electrons, and on the Amati correlation in GRBs.

arxiv-2209-01287.title: Critical points of WAdS/CFT and higher-curvature gravity
arxiv-2209-01287.creator: Gerónimo Caselli, Gaston Giribet, Andrés Goya
arxiv-2209-01287.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Gerónimo Caselli, Gaston Giribet, Andrés Goya. WAdS/WCFT correspondence is an interesting realization of non-AdS holography. It relates 3-dimensional Warped-Anti-de Sitter (WAdS 3 ) spaces to a special class of 2-dimensional quantum field theory with chiral scaling symmetry that acts only on right-moving modes. The latter are often called Warped Conformal Field Theories (WCFT 2 ), and their existence makes WAdS/WCFT particularly interesting as a tool to investigate a new type of 2-dimensional conformal structure.

arxiv-2306-05894.title: Mode mixing and losses in misaligned microcavities
arxiv-2306-05894.creator: William J Hughes, Thomas H Doherty, Jacob A Blackmore, Peter Horak, Joseph F Goodwin
arxiv-2306-05894.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by William J Hughes, Thomas H Doherty, Jacob A Blackmore, Peter Horak, Joseph F Goodwin. We present a study on the optical losses of Fabry-Pérot cavities subject to realistic transverse mirror misalignment. We consider mirrors of the two most prevalent surface forms: idealised spherical depressions, and Gaussian profiles generated by laser ablation.

arxiv-2410-05193.title: RevisEval : Improving LLM-as-a-Judge via Response-Adapted References
arxiv-2410-05193.creator: Qiyuan Zhang, Yufei Wang, Tiezheng Yu, Yuxin Jiang, Chuhan Wu, Liangyou Li, Yasheng Wang, Xin Jiang, Lifeng Shang, Ruiming Tang, Fuyuan Lyu, Chen Ma
arxiv-2410-05193.description: Abstract With significant efforts in recent studies, LLM-as-a-Judge has become a cost-effective alternative to human evaluation for assessing text generation quality in a wide range of tasks. However, there still remains a reliability gap between LLM-as-a-Judge and human evaluation. One important reason is the lack of guided oracles in the evaluation process.

arxiv-2511-12827.title: Efficient Adversarial Malware Defense via Trust-Based Raw Override and Confidence-Adaptive Bit-Depth Reduction
arxiv-2511-12827.creator: Ayush Chaudhary, Sisir Doppalpudi
arxiv-2511-12827.description: Abstract The deployment of robust malware detection systems in big data environments requires careful consideration of both security effectiveness and computational efficiency. While recent advances in adversarial defenses have demonstrated strong robustness improvements, they often introduce computational overhead ranging from 4 × 4\times to 22 × 22\times , which presents significant challenges for production systems processing millions of samples daily.

We mined seven SRlncRNAs (SOX9‐AS1, LINC01152, AC005152.3, RP11‐161 M6.2, RP5‐968 J1.1, RP11‐351 J23.1 and RP11‐666A20.

pmc-11571465.description: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the effects of contrast heat and cold pressure therapy (CHCP) on muscle tone, elasticity, stiffness, perfusion unit, and muscle fatigue indices after plyometric training consisting of five sets of jumping on a 50-cm high box until exhaustion. A prospective, randomized, controlled single-blind study design was used.

pmc-11598860.title: Pathological Study of Demyelination with Cellular Reactions in the Cerebellum of Dogs Infected with Canine Distemper Virus
pmc-11598860.creator: José Manuel Verdes, Camila Larrañaga, Guillermo Godiño, Belén Varela, Victoria Yozzi, Victoria Iribarnegaray, Luis Delucchi, Kanji Yamasaki
pmc-11598860.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The purpose of this study was to examine the relationship between demyelination and cellular reactions in the cerebellum of Canine Distemper Virus (CDV)-infected dogs. We subdivided the disease staging by adding the degree of demyelination determined by Luxol Fast Blue staining to the previously reported disease staging from the acute stage to the chronic stage, and investigated the relationship between demyelination in the cerebellum and the number and histological changes in astroglia, microglia, and Purkinje cells in each stage.

pmc-12553017.creator: Aron Alakmeh, Vittorio Stumpo, Stefanos Voglis, Antonio Spinello, Victor Gabriel El-Hajj, Adrian Elmi-Terander, Luca Regli, Carlo Serra, Victor E Staartjes, Flavio Vasella
pmc-12553017.description: IntroductionChronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) frequently recurs. Numerous studies have investigated the influence of various factors on the likelihood of recurrence, yet the potential influence of individual surgeon identity beyond general experience level remains unclear.Research questionTo evaluate whether surgeon-specific differences contribute to recurrence rates whilst accounting for standardized technique and known patient-/procedure-related factors.

pmc-12717194.title: High-efficiency tandem DSSCs based on tailored naphthalene sensitizers for indoor DSSC efficiency above 25%
pmc-12717194.creator: Mohamed R Elmorsy, Samar M Mohammed, Basant A Mohamed, Ahmed H Moustafa, Safa A Badawy
pmc-12717194.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) are among the most promising photovoltaic technologies for both outdoor and indoor energy harvesting due to their low cost and spectral versatility. In this work, a new series of organic donor–π–acceptor (D–π–A) sensitizers (BAM-1–BAM-4) featuring a naphthalene donor and a phenyl-pyrazole π-bridge were designed to explore how structural variations in electron-withdrawing acceptors influence light absorption, charge transfer, and device efficiency.

Methods: DPSC cultures were obtained from third molars extracted from healthy volunteers and characterized by flow cytometry.

pmc-13038409.title: Improving few-shot named entity recognition for large language models using structured dynamic prompting with retrieval augmented generation
pmc-13038409.creator: Yao Ge, Yuting Guo, Sudeshna Das, Abeed Sarker
pmc-13038409.description: Biomedical named entity recognition (NER) is a high-utility natural language processing task, and large language models (LLMs) show promise in few-shot settings. In this article, we address performance challenges for few-shot biomedical NER by investigating innovative prompting strategies involving retrieval-augmented generation.

BackgroundAdvances in endocrine therapies for hormone receptor (HR)-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (ABC) continue to transform care and significantly improve patient outcomes. However, the integration of molecular and clinical risk stratification into guiding individualized treatment selection remains a key challenge.

pmc-13188441.title: Effectiveness of an education intervention in reducing self- and other-directed ageism: a pre-/post- pilot study
pmc-13188441.creator: L M O’Brien, M Mundy, N Cook, S Sabatini, R C Ambagtsheer
pmc-13188441.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ageism is a serious and growing social issue experienced throughout the world. While education interventions have been shown to effectively address ageism, accessible education interventions targeted to the general public are few. Consequently, this study aimed to evaluate the impact of a freely available, short, self-directed online ageism course (‘Challenging Ageism’) in reducing self- and other-directed ageism amongst the general public.
